The '''2011–12''' season of the '''[[Belgian Pro League]]''' (also known as ''Jupiler Pro League'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 109th season of top-tier football in [[Belgium]]. It began on 29 July 2011 with the first match of the regular season and ended in May 2012 with the last matches of the playoff rounds. The defending champions were [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]], who this time ended in third position, while the competition was won by [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]], who clenched the title after a 1–1 draw against [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]] with two games left to play in the Championship Playoff.

==Teams==

===Team changes===
During the [[2010–11 Belgian Pro League|previous season]], on 23 April 2011, [[S. du Pays de Charleroi|Charleroi]] were relegated as a result of a 2–2 draw at home to [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] in the [[2010–11 Belgian Pro League#Relegation Playoff|relegation playoff]], making it impossible to overtake them in the standings. This ended a spell of 26 consecutive seasons of being at the top level of Belgian football, with only [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]], [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]] and [[Standard Liège]] being present for more years.<ref name=charleroi>{{cite news |title= Charleroi relegates to Second Division|url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1006478|publisher=sporza.be |date=2011-04-23|language=nl}}</ref> As winner of the relegation playoff, [[K.A.S. Eupen|Eupen]] avoided direct relegation, but was still forced to play the [[Belgian Second Division final rounds 2011–20#2011|Second Division final round]] together with second division teams [[Lommel United]], [[Waasland-Beveren]] and [[RAEC Mons (1910)|Mons]] for the final spot in first division. However, after losing four matches in a row, Eupen was also relegated on 19 May 2011<ref name=eupenrelegated>{{cite news |title= Promotion to First Division gets closer for Mons|url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1028110|publisher=sporza.be |date=2011-05-19|language=nl}}</ref> after just one season at the top level. In the final match between Mons and Waasland-Beveren, Mons eventually came out as winner of the final round and took the place of Eupen.<ref name=monspromoted>{{cite news |title= Promotion to First Division gets closer for Mons|url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1034742|publisher=sporza.be |date=2011-05-29|language=nl}}</ref>

On 24 April 2011, just one day after the relegation of Charleroi, [[Oud-Heverlee Leuven]] was promoted after securing the title in the [[2010–11 Belgian Second Division|Second Division]] and as a result, the city of [[Leuven]] now has a first division team again for the first time in 61 years.<ref name=ohleuven>{{cite news |title= Leuven has a first division team again after 61 years|url=http://www.sporza.be/permalink/1.1009994|publisher=sporza.be |date=2011-04-24|language=nl}}</ref>

==Championship playoff==
The points obtained during the regular season were halved (and rounded up) before the start of the playoff. As a result, the teams started with the following points before the playoff: Anderlecht 34 points, Club Brugge 31, Gent 28, Standard 26, Genk 23 and Kortrijk 23.

The winners of both playoff groups competed in a two-legged match to play the fourth-placed team of the championship playoff, called [[#Testmatches Europa League|Testmatch]]. ==Relegation playoff==
The teams finishing in the last two positions Westerlo and Sint-Truiden, faced each other in the relegation playoff. Westerlo started with a three-point bonus and home advantage for finishing above Sint-Truiden during the regular season. Although the teams were scheduled to play each other 5 times, Westerlo forced the decision already after four matches making the last match obsolete. Thereby, Sint-Truiden was relegated and Westerlo was allowed to play the relegation playoffs with the teams from the [[Belgian Second Division|Second Division]].
